Midweek, basic rules for tag checks
This section describes the main rule first, then the reasons
Companion Animal Travel Desk Tag Check Standards

This section sets the baseline for tag checks so staff can confirm traveler records, reduce avoidable delays, and protect each companion animal throughout the service journey. The desk welcomes questions in a warm professional tone and gives clear guidance from booking through pickup.

The main rule is to verify every tag against the current booking record before any further action is taken. Staff must compare the animal identifier, traveler details, and routing notes with care, and they must speak plainly if anything does not match. A calm and respectful approach helps the traveler remain confident while the desk resolves the matter. If a tag is unclear, damaged, or missing, the staff member should pause the handoff and report the concern at once.

When a record is complete, the staff member should confirm the tag status in the service file and continue with the next step only after the review is finished. If the desk receives a traveler with more than one companion animal, each tag must be checked separately to prevent confusion. The senior coordinator oversees daily service decisions and reviews unusual cases so that service remains consistent and fair. Staff should not guess at a tag reading or rely on memory when the record is available.

If a discrepancy appears, staff must follow a calm stepwise review. First, they should recheck the booking details and the physical tag. Next, they should seek a second review from the senior coordinator. If the issue still cannot be resolved, they should advise the traveler that the matter is under review and continue care without unnecessary delay. This approach protects the animal, respects the traveler, and supports the standards of Aurelia Skyways.

At all times, staff should document the outcome in clear language, keep the interaction courteous, and maintain focus on the well-being of the animal. Contact the senior coordinator or the Companion Animal Travel Desk for guidance when a tag issue cannot be settled at the counter.
